fieldMarks: Small; males 21-30 mm, females 22-33 mm snout-vent; light gray to tan, brown or black with blackish stripes or spots in three rows.
White line along the pointed snout and upper lip, dark band through the eye; skin with small warts.
No stripe on the rear of the thighs; rear toes weakly webbed.
Breeding males have a dark (olive or rusty orange) throat.
behavior: Mostly nocturnal, though males may call by day around dusk; breeds from fall to early spring (winter peak) in the north and in any month in Florida, often after heavy rain.
Seldom found outside the breeding season; burrows or hides when conditions are poor; sexually mature at 1 year and few live longer.
Opportunistic insectivore; moves between wetlands and upland pine forest.
habitat: Pine flatwoods, pine-oak forests, sandhills and disturbed areas; breeds in flooded grassy depressions, roadside ditches, pond margins and temporary pools.
range: Southeastern coast of the United States: Florida, southern Georgia, eastern South Carolina and North Carolina (north to the Tar and Pamlico Rivers), west to southern Alabama and Mississippi, with a disjunct population in southeastern Virginia. Not in Canada.
